text: Write an enum carrying per-constant data, and switch over it exhaustively. Fill in the three blanks.
explanation: Verified: `Coat Coat`. Two things at once — the constants carry their own data, so there is no parallel lookup table to keep aligned, and the switch has no `default`, so adding a fourth constant turns it into a compile error listing exactly where to update. Delete one case and the program stops building, which is the check that makes an enum better than `int` constants.
